name: Fondazione Prada
key_features: Former distillery buildings joined by new galleries, a tower and a small house clad in gold leaf.

name: Grand Mosque of Bursa
key_features: Interior covered by twenty domes in four rows of five on twelve columns, with a central fountain.

name: Hajj Terminal, King Abdulaziz International Airport
key_features: Hundreds of fibreglass tent modules on steel pylons shade a vast open-air terminal.

name: Hiroshima City Museum of Contemporary Art
key_features: Row of storehouse-like roofs; materials rise from stone to tile to aluminium round an empty circular plaza.

name: Jerusalem Theatre
by: Michael Nadler, Shulamit Nadler and Shmuel Bixson
key_features: Combines sculptural exposed concrete with traditional Jerusalem stone construction; opened 1971.

name: Johannesburg City Hall
key_features: Edwardian Baroque with an Ionic portico and tower; clad in Free State freestone.

name: Lijnbaan
key_features: Described as Europe's first purpose-built pedestrian shopping street, built to rebuild Rotterdam after 1940.

name: Maison à Bordeaux
key_features: Three stacked houses; a 3 x 3.5 m lift platform moves through all levels for the wheelchair-using owner.

name: Reggio Emilia AV Mediopadana station
key_features: Calatrava's high-speed station on the Milan-Bologna line, with two side platforms.

name: Moscow State University Main Building
key_features: Stepped central tower with symmetrical wings, a whole campus housed in one building.

name: National Library Building
key_features: Two blocks linked by bridges round a shaded open atrium, with sun-shading blades and sky gardens.

name: Palazzo di Giustizia, Milan
key_features: Reinforced-concrete courthouse with a restrained exterior, a 61 m corner tower and art by Sironi and Melotti.

name: Philharmonie de Paris
key_features: A shell of interlocking bird-shaped aluminium tiles rises to a rooftop belvedere above the park.

name: Remai Modern
key_features: 11,582 m² art museum on the South Saskatchewan River; opened October 2017.

name: Sappaya-Sapasathan (Thai Parliament)
key_features: Thai pagoda at the centre with separate halls for the House of Representatives and Senate.

name: Sheldon Museum of Art
key_features: A travertine temple of tapered columns and arches around a grand central hall.

name: Tomb of Nader Shah
key_features: Rough granite mass under a sharp angular canopy, with bronze riders of the shah's army.

name: Brazilian Press Association Building (ABI)
key_features: Office block wrapped in fixed concrete sun-breakers, among the first brise-soleil facades ever built.

name: American Republic Insurance Company Headquarters
key_features: Insurance headquarters completed in 1965; listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2015.

name: Anzeiger-Hochhaus
key_features: Dark clinker-brick tower with vertical piers, topped by a copper dome that once held a planetarium.

name: Athens Conservatoire
key_features: A long grid-framed concrete block over an open ground floor, part of an unfinished cultural centre.

name: Bahrain National Museum
key_features: Linked white travertine-clad volumes set on the waterfront around a central hall.

name: Bakhmetevsky Bus Garage
key_features: A parallelogram plan lets buses drive through without reversing, under Shukhov's steel trusses.

name: Battersea Power Station
by: J. Theo Halliday and Giles Gilbert Scott
key_features: One of the world's largest brick buildings, with original Art Deco interior fittings.

name: Beit Beirut (Barakat Building)
key_features: Ochre Deir el Qamar limestone building; Kozah added two storeys in 1932; now a museum and cultural centre.

name: Belém Cultural Center
key_features: Stone-clad blocks set along internal streets and courtyards, like a small fortified town.

name: Brücke Museum
key_features: Low single-storey galleries grouped around an inner courtyard at the edge of the Grunewald forest.

name: Bullitt Center
key_features: Rooftop array of 575 panels and 26 geothermal wells about 400 ft deep.

name: Burrell Collection
by: Barry Gasson, John Meunier and Brit Andresen
key_features: A glass gallery runs along a woodland edge, with medieval stone portals set into its sandstone walls.

name: Butte-aux-Cailles swimming pool
key_features: One of the oldest swimming pools in Paris, on place Paul-Verlaine in the 13th arrondissement, designed by Louis Bonnier.

name: Café Seerose
key_features: Thin hyperbolic concrete shells fold out like water-lily petals over a café on the Havel.

name: Cairo Tower
key_features: A concrete tower in a lattice shell evoking a lotus plant, topped by an observation deck.

name: Campus Palmas Altas (Sevilla)
key_features: A group of seven buildings by Richard Rogers and Luis Vidal Arquitectos, once Abengoa's headquarters.

name: Casa de Vidro
key_features: Glass-walled living floor on slender pilotis over a forested slope, with a tree rising through a central void.

name: Centro Cultural Gabriela Mistral
key_features: Rebuilt conference centre with perforated weathering-steel volumes and plazas cut through the block.

name: China Pavilion, Expo 2010
key_features: Inverted pyramid of stacked red beams cantilevers outward, modelled on dougong timber brackets.

name: Cibona Tower
key_features: Façade of dark steel, reflective glass and black granite; rim carried by 26 concrete pylons; built 1987.

name: Concertgebouw
key_features: Shoebox-shaped main hall, famed for its acoustics, behind a classical brick-and-stone front.

name: Copenhagen Police Headquarters (Politigården)
key_features: Severe Nordic-classical block on a triangular plan wrapped around a great round colonnaded courtyard.

name: De Vonk
key_features: Symmetrical brick holiday house with Van Doesburg's coloured brick and tile patterns at door and hall.

name: Echigo-Matsunoyama Museum of Natural Science (Kyororo)
key_features: Natural science museum noted by The Architectural Review in 2004; a Tezuka Architects work of 2003.

name: Edificio Panamericano
key_features: Long apartment slab raised on V-shaped concrete pilotis, facing the river at Buceo.

name: Humble Administrator's Garden
key_features: Pavilions, galleries and rockeries set around ponds so views unfold along a winding path.

name: Hungerburgbahn stations
key_features: Double-curved glass shells float over concrete plinths at each funicular station like frozen ice.

name: John Deere World Headquarters
key_features: Corporate headquarters opened in 1964; won the AIA Twenty-five Year Award.

name: Kino Babylon
key_features: A 1928–29 listed cinema by Hans Poelzig in the Neue Sachlichkeit style, restored in 1999–2001.

name: Maersk Tower
key_features: Research tower on a low landscaped base, wrapped in copper shutters that move with the sun.

name: Napier Street Housing
key_features: Eleven terrace-like dwellings with roof terraces; big brick faces hover over the street corners.

name: National Library of Brazil
key_features: Eclectic neoclassical and Art Nouveau design with ornaments by Eliseu Visconti.

name: Nira House (Leek House)
key_features: Roof ridge planted with a row of leeks in pots; walls of rough-split timber and hand-finished plaster.

name: Palacio de Aguas Corrientes
key_features: Water-pumping palace covered in about 300,000 majolica tiles.

name: Thanks-Giving Square
key_features: Sits about 15 ft below street level; chapel spiral rises 90 ft with the Glory Window.

name: Theatro Municipal de São Paulo
by: Ramos de Azevedo, Cláudio Rossi, Domiziano Rossi
key_features: Modelled on the Palais Garnier; venue of the 1922 Week of Modern Art.

name: Toho Gakuen School of Music
key_features: Concrete lesson rooms spaced apart by small courtyard-like gaps, with glass corners that let views and sound through.

name: Vasa Museum
key_features: Museum for the 17th-century warship Vasa; the design won a competition of 384 entries.

name: Wells Fargo Center
key_features: César Pelli's 774-foot Minneapolis tower, a modernised Art Deco design that echoes nearby towers.

name: Circular School, Agios Dimitrios
key_features: A three-storey disc of classrooms round a central core, its south half ringed by louvred eaves at every floor.

name: Allen Memorial Art Museum
key_features: An Oberlin College art museum founded in 1917, holding over 15,000 works.

name: Allianz Arena
key_features: ETFE cushion skin, lit red, blue or white, wraps the stadium bowl.

name: Allianz Tower (Il Dritto)
key_features: Fifty floors from eight six-storey modules, with a slightly curved triple-glass facade and panoramic lifts.

name: Aomori Museum of Art
key_features: White brick box hovers over trench galleries cut into the ground, like an excavation.

name: Aquarium of Genoa
key_features: Built for Expo '92 on the old port; 70 tanks hold about 6 million litres of water.

name: Argo Contemporary Art Museum
key_features: Old brick brewery turned art museum; a new frame carries floors and pitched roofs that float above the walls.

name: Arizona Biltmore Hotel
key_features: Precast 'Biltmore Blocks' made on site from desert sand; Frank Lloyd Wright consulted on the textile-block system.

name: Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center
key_features: Eight one-storey houses with pitched roofs stacked into a tower, screened by timber louvres.

name: Astrup Fearnley Museum
key_features: Curved glass roof on laminated timber beams sweeps over gallery buildings by the fjord.

name: Auckland Art Gallery
key_features: Tree-like kauri timber canopies over a glazed extension that opens the gallery to the park.

name: Austin Hall
key_features: The first building purpose-built for an American law school and the first home of Harvard Law School.

name: Autrique House
key_features: Horta's first town house: a modest stone front with the first hints of his Art Nouveau ironwork.

name: Avala Tower
key_features: 204.68 m transmission tower on Mount Avala, finished 1965, destroyed in 1999 and reconstructed; reopened April 2010.

name: Avicenna Mausoleum
key_features: A tower of twelve concrete columns tapering upward, modelled on the Gonbad-e Qabus tomb tower.

name: Ayala Museum
key_features: Six-storey building of granite, steel and glass.

name: Bahá'í House of Worship, Kampala
key_features: Domed temple 39 m high, with an Italian mosaic-tiled dome; stone, doors and benches from Uganda; dedicated 1961.

name: Bank of Georgia headquarters
key_features: Concrete blocks stacked crosswise on cores like a log pile, leaving open voids and free ground.

name: Bat Yam City Hall
key_features: An inverted stepped pyramid of concrete around an inner court, with a faceted polyhedral roof.

name: Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library
key_features: Translucent marble panels in a Vierendeel frame filter light onto a glass-walled book tower.

name: Bharat Bhavan
key_features: Arts centre stepped down a hillside to the Upper Lake as terraces and sunken courts, with an open-air theatre.

name: Bloch Building, Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art
key_features: Five translucent glass lenses step down a sculpture park, lighting galleries set into the slope.

name: Bosco Verticale
key_features: Two towers carrying about 900 trees on staggered balconies.

name: Bracken House
by: Albert Richardson; central part redesigned by Michael Hopkins and Partners
key_features: First post-war building listed in England; pink sandstone and bronze, centre redesigned by Hopkins 1988-92.

name: British Library
by: Colin St John Wilson, MJ Long
key_features: Stepped red-brick masses round a raised piazza; inside, the King's Library rises as a tall glass tower.

name: Byker Wall
key_features: A long perimeter block with small north windows shelters colourful low-rise housing and timber balconies.

name: Cape Town City Hall
by: Henry Austin Reid and Frederick George Green
key_features: Edwardian city hall of honey-coloured limestone imported from Bath, with a clock tower and carillon.

name: Cardboard Cathedral
key_features: Large cardboard tubes form an A-frame on shipping containers, ending in a triangular coloured-glass wall.

name: Casa Klotz
key_features: A white timber box, 6 x 6 x 12 m, nearly closed to the south and opened to the beach with a double-height living room.

name: Casa Rotalinti
key_features: A Brutalist house by Aurelio Galfetti in Bellinzona, built by 1961 and listed as regionally important.

name: Cathedral of Saint Mary of the Assumption
by: Pietro Belluschi and Pier Luigi Nervi
key_features: Four hyperbolic paraboloid concrete shells rise from a square base to meet in a cross of glass.

name: Centro de Exposições do Centro Administrativo da Bahia
key_features: 52 m concrete building held about 5 m above the ground by cables from two side towers.

name: Century Plaza Towers
key_features: Twin triangular towers clad in aluminium with narrow vertical windows.

name: Chapel of the Holy Cross
by: August K. Strotz and Richard Hein (Anshen & Allen)
key_features: Built into red rock buttes; roughly 90-ft iron cross is also structural, in sandblasted 1-ft concrete walls.

name: Château Frontenac
key_features: Châteauesque railway hotel of 18 floors, opened 1893; National Historic Site since 1981.

name: Choux de Créteil
key_features: Ten round towers whose balconies are curved concrete petals, like the leaves of a cabbage.

name: Christian Science Plaza
key_features: Concrete Colonnade Building, 26-storey tower and Sunday School set round a 210 m reflecting pool.

name: Concord Pavilion
key_features: Open-air amphitheatre: one broad steel-truss roof over the seats, with a lawn rising up the hill behind.

name: CopenHill
key_features: Waste-to-energy plant whose sloping roof is a public ski slope, with a climbing wall on the facade.

name: Danish Maritime Museum
key_features: Galleries wrap an old dry dock below ground, crossed by sloping bridges over the empty basin.

name: Deere & Company Administrative Center
key_features: Office floors wrapped in a frame of weathering steel and deep sunshades, spanning a wooded ravine.

name: Dennis Chavez Federal Building
key_features: Steel-framed high-rise faced with polished granite; lobby uses New Mexico marble.

name: Design Research Building
key_features: A shop with no solid walls: clear glass hung between thin concrete floor slabs, so the store becomes a lit display.

name: Dialogue Centre Przełomy
key_features: History museum hidden under a city square whose paving rises into slopes; a hard-edged pavilion marks one corner.
